hub.title: Customs
hub.tagline: Pay the right duty. Not a franc more, not a franc less.
hub.intro: On a single real customs declaration, four items out of ten were misclassified: a voltage "regulator" declared as a refrigerator, chairs as furniture, new clothes as second-hand clothing. These tools show what you really owe, before you buy.
hub.simulatorDesc: What customs will charge for a product, line by line, before you buy.
hub.searchDesc: Using market words: hair extensions, second-hand clothes, okada, 手机…
hub.walletCardDesc: Simulate a product's duties and taxes before paying your supplier.
hub.facts: The calculations reproduce the CAMCIS assessment to the franc on real declarations.

notes.freight_missing: Freight is not counted. Customs adds it to the value: every franc of freight is taxed like the goods.
notes.vehicle_other_rule: The 2026 finance law provides {{rate}}% excise for this vehicle (CAMCIS still applies the former rule): {{total}} F of duties and taxes instead of {{current}} F.
notes.tec_40: The ECCAS common tariff in force since 1 January 2026 may raise this product to 40%: that would be {{total}} F instead of {{current}} F. Have the rate confirmed in the CAMCIS integrated tariff.
notes.phones: Phones: the 2023 finance law (art. 7) provides a 50% abatement on the value, and CAMCIS links the tax to the IMEI since 2026. Not applied here: confirm with your declarant.
notes.env_tax_plastic: Environmental tax on plastic articles (2026 finance law): 5% of the value, capped at 1,000 F per unit. Not counted here.
notes.insurance_estimated: Insurance estimated at 0.5%: insurance of imported goods is compulsory in Cameroon, with a locally licensed insurer (law no. 75-14).
notes.precompte_niu: Without a NIU, the précompte is 10% instead of 2% for a company on the real regime. A tax ID (NIU) is free at the tax office.
notes.di_rvc: Above 2,000,000 F FOB: import declaration (DI) on e-GUCE before shipment, then SGS verification certificate (RVC). Without them, the fine is 25% of the value (2026 finance law).
notes.sgs_invoice: Ask your supplier to upload the final invoice to export-cm.sgs.com as soon as the goods ship. Without it, SGS may retain a value three times higher — it happened on a Toyota Fortuner: 2,311,829 F too much.
notes.domiciliation: Above 5,000,000 F, the import must be domiciled with a bank. Pay your supplier with Bonzini: the payment proof establishes the price actually paid (CEMAC customs code, art. 30).
notes.code_check: Check that the code on the declaration describes your goods, not a word that looks like it: a "regulator" declared as a refrigerator cost 35,779 F too much on 150,000 F.
